Step 2: Step size |x_{n+1} - x_n| < eps: misleading if convergence is very slow (step small even far from root).
Step 3: 2.
Step 4: Residual |f(x_n)| < eps: misleading if curve is very flat (f'(r) approx 0, large error in x despite small f).

intermediate_values.analytical_result: Use combined criterion: |x_{n+1} - x_n| < eps1 AND |f(x_{n+1})| < eps2.

final_answer: Use combined criterion: |x_{n+1} - x_n| < eps1 AND |f(x_{n+1})| < eps2.
verification: Verified against standard numerical analysis theorems (Burden & Faires, NPTEL).
common_mistake: Assuming quadratic convergence holds unconditionally for multiple roots or zero derivatives.

problem: Compare Bisection, Regula-Falsi, Secant, and Newton-Raphson in terms of: 1. Order of convergence, 2. Number of function evaluations per step, 3. Guarantee of convergence.
step_by_step_calculation: Step 1: Bisection: Order 1, 1 eval/step, Guaranteed if f(a)f(b)<0.
Step 2: Regula-Falsi: Order ~1.6 (can slow to 1), 1 eval/step, Guaranteed if bracketed.
Step 3: Secant: Order 1.618, 1 eval/step, Not guaranteed.
Step 4: Newton-Raphson: Order 2 (simple root), 2 evals/step (f and f'), Not guaranteed (local convergence only).
